mcp.title: MCP agents
mcp.subtitle: Let AI agents chat with you securely
mcp.intro: An MCP token lets an AI agent (e.g. a coding assistant) create a chat and bind it to your account. Your app then joins it automatically — it shows up in the hidden "MCP chats" row on the home screen.
mcp.empty: No tokens yet. Mint one to let an agent create a chat bound to you.
mcp.secret_warning: This is the only time the token is shown. Paste it into the agent's MCP_TOKEN configuration.
mcp.revoke_confirm_body: Agents using this token can no longer bind new chats to you. Chats already bound stay as they are.

backup.title: Backup & recovery
backup.subtitle: Protect your identity against a wipe
backup.intro: Chattr accounts are anonymous with no email recovery. If you lose or reinstall the app, your identity and keys are gone for good. Create an encrypted backup and keep it somewhere safe (e.g. your password manager or iCloud/Files).
backup.footnote: The backup contains your identity and encryption keys — but not your message history. Restoring gets you back into all your chats and able to read new messages. Anyone with the file AND your passphrase can take over your account, so guard both.
backup.restore_confirm_body: This replaces the identity and keys on this device with the ones from the backup file. Only do this on a fresh install or a device you want to take over your account.
backup.restore_done_body: Your identity and keys were restored. Please fully close and reopen Chattr so your chats reload.
backup.passphrase_hint: You'll need this exact passphrase to restore. It can't be recovered if you forget it.

recovery.title: Recovery phrase
recovery.subtitle: Recover your account on a new device
recovery.intro: Turn your anonymous account into something you can restore. We generate a 24-word recovery phrase; keep it safe and you can sign back in on any device — even after a wipe or reinstall. Your identity stays anonymous (no email, no phone).
recovery.footnote: The phrase recovers your identity and gets you back into all your chats. It does not restore old message history. Anyone who has your phrase can take over your account — treat it like a master password.
recovery.phrase_warning: Write these 24 words down in order and store them in a secure password manager. This is shown only once and cannot be recovered if you lose it.
recovery.confirm_saved: I've saved my recovery phrase somewhere safe
recovery.active_subtitle: You have a recovery phrase set up for this account.
recovery.regenerate_confirm_body: This generates a NEW 24-word phrase and makes your current one invalid. If you've saved the old phrase somewhere, it will stop working. Continue?

identity.title: Verification
identity.explain: Compare this number with {} over a trusted channel (in person or on a call). If it matches, your connection is end-to-end secure — no server sits in the middle.
identity.unknown_explain: {} hasn't published an identity key yet (older client). Verification becomes possible once their app is updated.
identity.changed_explain: {}'s identity key has changed. This happens after a reinstall or account recovery — but could also indicate an attack. Compare the safety number before trusting the new key.
identity.accepted_snack: New key accepted — not verified yet
identity.scan_hint: Or scan {}'s QR code for automatic verification.
identity.my_key_missing: Your identity key hasn't been published yet — others can't verify you until it is.
identity.pending_peer_info: {}'s profile becomes visible once the chat request is accepted. Verification is possible after that.
identity.my_key_lost: Your identity key can no longer be read on this device. Your messages therefore go out unsigned — the people you write to cannot prove they came from you.
identity.regenerate_confirm_body:
You will get a new identity key. All your contacts will see "safety number changed" and have to verify you again.

Old messages addressed to the lost key do not become readable again.
identity.regenerate_done: New identity key created and published
identity.regenerate_failed: Could not create a new key

server_status.offline_body: Your messages are encrypted on this device and all still there. Only the connection is missing — everything resumes on its own once the server answers again.

push_media_kind.enable_hint: Shows “sent a photo” instead of “New message”. In exchange, Google's or Apple's push service learns whether it was a photo, a video, an audio file or a file — not the content, not the filename. Off: the notification stays generic. In the app you see the type regardless; no third party is involved there.
